headline: CROCS PUT A LIVE SHOPPING STREAM ON STAGE AT A MARKETING CONFERENCE YESTERDAY.  THREE THOUSAND PEOPLE WATCHED IT AND IT SOLD 200 ITEMS IN TWELVE MINUTES
deck: An audience of 3,000 is a number that gets a social post quietly killed in most review meetings.  Crocs has built an estimated 52.4 million dollars of TikTok Shop sales on that kind of audience, and the thing its chief brand officer says produced it is not budget. tldr: Crocs sold 200 items in twelve minutes to about 3,000 live viewers on stage at Brandweek, on top of an estimated 52.4 million dollars of TikTok Shop sales in the twelve months to April and a 31-day, 744-hour livestream that tripled its follower count.  Book one live shopping stream in the next three weeks and judge it on items sold per minute rather than viewers, with the target written down before you start.

Emplifi reviewed more than 520,000 posts from 3,791 Instagram brand profiles and found creator-published collaborations consistently outperform both brand posts and brand-published ones, with creator-published collabs reaching more than five times the amplification of posts with no collaboration in ecommerce and retail.  Sort your last ten collaboration posts by who pressed publish, and rewrite the next contract so the creator posts and invites you on.

Business Insider's inside account of the Good Good collapse confirms the ad went through review on both sides, with Callaway saying its process was inadequate and its chief executive saying the company should not have approved it — after a 56-second spot cost two executives, four retailers, a PGA Tour title sponsorship and a television series.  Add one person to your next approval who has had nothing explained to them and ask only what they think they just watched.

The European Commission adopted the KIDS Act this morning, barring social media platforms from accessing under-13s, setting 15 as the age for opening your own account, and reversing the burden of proof so platforms must show they are safe by design.  Add a line to your European creator contracts asking partners to state their audience age composition from their own analytics, and start collecting the answers now.

IAB Australia's new survey of 1,079 online shoppers puts large audience or follower size last of seven trust factors at 20.5 percent, behind proven track record at 45.8 and independence from brands at 34.7, while 44 percent say they are less likely to act once they know a post is paid.  Score your next creator shortlist on years covering the subject and whether they have ever published a negative verdict in your category, and let those override follower count.

Marvel's Wolverine peaked at 268,500 concurrent viewers with 3.46 million hours watched across 15,300 channels, and sponsored streams took 13.9 percent of those hours against a usual ceiling near 10 — while the three biggest streamers on the game ran no sponsorship disclosure at all.  Ask every launch partner in writing whether they had already planned to cover the thing you are paying them for, and move the spare budget into mid-sized channels in your two biggest non-English markets.

Meta put links in Instagram posts and Reels behind a subscription at four a month for 49.99 dollars rising to twelve for 499, added permission expiry dates and one-click music stripping to its Creator Marketing Hub, and opens sponsored creator livestreams on Instagram from 29 September.  Price your real monthly link volume against the three tiers before subscribing, and brief one creator livestream to sponsor in the first fortnight after the 29th.
